name: Honasa Consumer Ltd
title: Honasa Consumer Ltd - 544014 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 revenue up 28% YoY to INR682 crore with EBITDA 11.3% and PAT INR69 crore, but growth is demand-led brand execution with no supply-side or capacity disclosures; FY27 guidance is a 5-year high-teens CAGR.

triggers.label: Q4 revenue growth 28% YoY
triggers.quote: We've delivered 28% Y -o-Y growth with EBITDA scaling almost 2.5x over last year same quarter.

triggers.label: Calibrated price increases executed in Q1
triggers.quote: we have already executed some calibrated price increases in line with where we've also seen competition taking the price in crease the same

triggers.label: Distributor stocks at 25-30 days
triggers.quote: Our Direct Distributors stocks are also optimized between 25 to 30 days.

guidance.quote: we'll grow at a high-teens CAGR from the next 5 years' perspective

guidance.value: ~500 bps over 5 years (about 100 bps per year)
guidance.quote: over the next 5 years, we want to get 500 basis points better
we're fairly confident of delivering a double -digit CAGR on the brand from the next 5 years perspective
the Board has decided to reward shareholders with a dividend straight off with INR 3 per equity share

red_flags.quote: The reported growth, of course, contains the Flipkart adjustment that we have been talking about

summary.headline: Honasa Q4 FY26 revenue grew 28% YoY to INR682 crore with EBITDA at 11.3% (~2.5x YoY) and PAT of INR69 crore.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the third consecutive quarter of 20%+ growth, with revenue of INR682 crore, gross margin of 71.4% (up 70 bps YoY), EBITDA of INR77 crore (11.3%) and PAT of INR69 crore (10.2%). Management said growth was volume-led and includes the BTM Ventures acquisition, with reported growth depressed by the Flipkart revenue-recognition adjustment (like-for-like growth stated at 28%). The Board declared a first-ever main-year dividend of INR3 per share, about 50% of FY26 PAT (above INR200 crore), with a total cash payout of about INR98 crore. FY26 EBITDA margin was about 9.3%, with management reiterating roughly 100 bps annual improvement and 500 bps over five years.

financial_highlights.value: INR3 per equity share; total cash outgo about INR98 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Other expenses as % of revenue (Q4, like-for-like basis per CFO)
financial_highlights.change: vs about 22% in same quarter last year

segments.name: Mamaearth
segments.commentary: Brand grew at mid-teens in Q4; FY26 growth in double digits. Management targets double-digit CAGR over five years, with distribution expanding from about 200,000 outlets toward 0.5 million in 3-5 years. Online is also growing double digits.

segments.name: The Derma Co. (TDC)
segments.commentary: Continues as a star performer with double-digit EBITDA; face wash business almost doubled and Nielsen shows about 1% market share in face wash. Hero products are over 50% of brand sales. ARR above INR750 crore per prior disclosure.

segments.name: Reginald Men
segments.commentary: First consolidated quarter; brand grew 100%+ and doubled revenue YoY and crossed INR100 crore ARR (sixth brand above that mark). Excluding Reginald, like-for-like growth is 21%, with EBITDA impact about 30 bps.

segments.name: Younger brands (aggregate)
segments.commentary: Grew about 40% including Reginald, and 28%-plus excluding Reginald. Management said more than six brands now have INR100 crore-plus ARR.

segments.name: Focus categories
segments.commentary: Grew 35% YoY; contribution rose about 500 bps in one year. Focus categories receive more than 90% of investment. Products launched in the last year contributed about 7-8% of growth.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a high-teens revenue CAGR over the next five years, with some years above and some below.
EBITDA margin to expand about 100 bps per year, and at least 500 bps over five years (leverage from channel, brand and OpEx spend).
Price increases executed in Q1 FY27 to offset crude-linked PM/RM inflation; no further price hikes expected at current crude levels. Price increase quantum not disclosed.
Young brands expected to keep driving strong growth in FY27; no specific FY27 numbers given.
Dividend of INR3 per share; management said cash generation continues even after inorganic deployment.
capex_capacity: Direct distributor stock optimised at 25-30 days.
Distribution expansion in Top-100 cities; Reginald Men extending to e-commerce platforms this quarter and opening Maharashtra.
Management plans to build out new businesses and categories (men's skincare, nutraceuticals/ingestible inside-out beauty) and hired new leaders; no capex or capacity figures disclosed.
demand_pricing: Growth described as volume-led (underlying volume growth strong), not price-led.
Calibrated price increases taken in line with competitor moves; management said RPI remains competitive at its premium positioning.
Management said Derma Co. is the largest actives brand per Euromonitor and has the highest Nielsen share among active brands, responding to HUL's Minimalist push in offline.
GT channel described as one of the fastest-growing channels; quantum of GT revenue not disclosed.
Reported growth affected by Flipkart settlement and GT charges that reduced realisation; distribution fees removed from P&L.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and medium-term outlook for Mamaearth given offline penetration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is fairly confident of a double-digit CAGR for Mamaearth over five years, driven by share gains in face wash, shampoo and other focus categories plus distribution rising from about 200,000 to 0.5 million outlets.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth comes from products launched in the last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Products launched in the last one year contributed about 7-8% of growth; management now evaluates innovation on a three-year horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Reginald Men strategy and how is the like-for-like growth ex-Reginald?
qa_highlights.answer: Reginald is 98% sunscreen at acquisition; growth axes are distribution (extending to e-commerce now), new categories (face wash, serums) and geography (Maharashtra). Excluding Reginald, like-for-like growth is 21% with about 30 bps EBITDA impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is Aqualogica underperforming relative to TDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TDC is the brand targeted to reach INR1,000 crore and Aqualogica is younger; it will share more details as the brand becomes material.

qa_highlights.question: How is pricing positioned against inflation and competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Calibrated price hikes were executed in Q1 FY27 in line with competitors; no further hikes expected at current crude levels. Quantum was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Does 21% like-for-like growth exclude the Flipkart impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The 21% excludes Reginald only; Flipkart adjustment would need to be removed separately to get true like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the decline in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 other expenses are about 18% of revenue versus about 22% last year on a like-for-like basis, driven by scale and leverage plus removal of distribution charges from the P&L.

risks_watch: Reported revenue is depressed by the Flipkart revenue-recognition adjustment and GT charges; bottom-line impact is neutral but reported growth may look lower than underlying.
Reliance on the BTM Ventures and Reginald acquisitions: inorganic contribution inflates headline growth.
Competitive intensity in actives from HUL (Minimalist) in offline channels.
Input-cost pressure from crude and war-linked PM/RM inflation; management has not quantified price increases.
Management is building new businesses (men's, nutraceuticals) which could add complexity and cost; profitability timing not specified.
Aqualogica performance was not detailed; visibility limited to combined view for other brands.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and the TDC and Reginald trajectories, with strong emphasis on volume-led growth. Management was evasive on specifics: it declined to quantify price hikes, gave little on Aqualogica, and gave no FY27 numbers beyond multi-year CAGR targets.
key_quotes: this is the third consecutive quarter of 20% plus growth for the company
Underlying volume growth has been strong, so this growth has actually been driven by volume and not just price.
keeping in line with the promise that we will continue to improve our EBITDA by the tune of about 100 basis points every year
we are fairly confident of delivering our high-teens CAGR over the next 5 years that we've talked about

growth.why: Management guides to a high-teens revenue CAGR over the next five years (midpoint ~17.5%), backed by volume-led growth, a Q1 FY27 price increase, young brands and focus categories (+35% YoY), with distribution expansion (Mamaearth toward 0.5 million outlets in 3-5 years) but no specific capacity, capex or order figures.
